triggers: a kernel on NVIDIA Blackwell GeForce/workstation (RTX PRO 5000 / SM120) risks the '4. Wrapping all shapes in one new custom op' trap

payload.goal: Avoid a known trap on NVIDIA Blackwell GeForce/workstation (RTX PRO 5000 / SM120): 4. Wrapping all shapes in one new custom op

problem.statement: SM120 NVFP4 Decode GEMM Production Pitfalls -- 4. Wrapping all shapes in one new custom op

payload.attempted: Put C1 fallback and C2 Split-K behind the same new `torch.library.custom_op`, with C1 internally calling CUTLASS.
payload.lesson: Keep C1 on the original vLLM CUTLASS path. Intercept only the specific C2-like shapes that need Split-K.

established_fact.mechanism: "Same backend inside" is not the same CUDA Graph or compiler boundary.

payload.observed: Even when C1 math uses CUTLASS, the graph boundary and compilation surface differ from stock vLLM, which can perturb prompt exactness and make E2E debugging ambiguous.
payload.root_cause: "Same backend inside" is not the same CUDA Graph or compiler boundary.
